lint.message: `main` takes `payload`. The host executes this block verbatim as a script, so nothing ever calls `main` with an argument: a parameter writes an unconfirmed host mechanism into the artifact as a settled contract, and the value it names can never arrive. Caller data reaches the skill as a serialized JSON string in an environment variable -- read it inside `main` via `os.environ`.

The sample code consumes caller fields (`invoices`, `applicant_alias`, `itemCode`, `amount`) but never reads a runtime input from the environment, so nothing the caller sends can reach it. The host passes caller data as a serialized JSON string in a `credentials` entry, which arrives as an environment variable: declare that variable in `## Required Inputs` and read it with `os.environ`.

`leave_type` reaches a query with a contract that states its TYPE but not its VALUE DOMAIN. Give the legal values verbatim as they go on the wire, or the format/unit/casing, or say the field is free text. A caller working from the user's own words will send those words.

`reason` reaches a query with a contract that states its TYPE but not its VALUE DOMAIN. Give the legal values verbatim as they go on the wire, or the format/unit/casing, or say the field is free text. A caller working from the user's own words will send those words.

The sample code raises `ValueError`. A raise that is not `SystemExit` exits non-zero, which the host reads as a DEPLOYMENT failure. A missing caller input belongs in `[NEEDS_INFO]` + `SystemExit(0)`, and a business rejection belongs in the error taxonomy; only `aca_env` / `obo_token` absence may exit non-zero.

The sample code can print `[NEEDS_INFO] missing=CALENDAR_EVENTS`, but `CALENDAR_EVENTS` appears in neither `## Required Inputs` nor a section dedicated to the `[NEEDS_INFO]` contract. The caller has no way to learn what to send.

The sample code puts `reason` into a query, but `## Required Inputs` never names it. The caller has no way to learn the field exists, let alone which values it accepts.

A SQL statement raises `THROW` / `RAISERROR` but the executing call is not inside a `try`. The driver exception escapes and turns a business condition into a non-zero exit the host reports as a broken skill.

`main` takes `argv`. The host executes this block verbatim as a script, so nothing ever calls `main` with an argument: a parameter writes an unconfirmed host mechanism into the artifact as a settled contract, and the value it names can never arrive. Caller data reaches the skill as a serialized JSON string in an environment variable -- read it inside `main` via `os.environ`.

The sample code reads the runtime input `GRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN` from the environment but can never print `[NEEDS_INFO] missing=GRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN`. When the host omits it -- most often by putting the payload in the free-text `request` parameter instead of a `credentials` entry -- the caller gets no readable signal at all: the script exits silently or crashes on a value that was never there.

The sample code reads the runtime input `DEFAULT_BUILDING` from the environment but can never print `[NEEDS_INFO] missing=DEFAULT_BUILDING`. When the host omits it -- most often by putting the payload in the free-text `request` parameter instead of a `credentials` entry -- the caller gets no readable signal at all: the script exits silently or crashes on a value that was never there.

The caller is asked to send `GRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN` in `credentials`, but EAA discards that key: `GRAPH_ACCESS_TOKEN` is an OBO_SCOPE_REGISTRY key, injected by the platform's OBO exchange. The value never reaches the script. Rename the input.
